topStories.headline: City Approves Marina Safeway Towers; Opponents Immediately File Amended Federal Suit
topStories.dek: San Francisco's Planning Department granted final approval to Align Real Estate's 848-unit redevelopment on November 6, and opponents escalated their federal lawsuit six days later, alleging the city stripped its own hazmat safeguards to speed the project through.
topStories.body:
San Francisco's Planning Department formally signed off on Align Real Estate's plan to replace the Marina Safeway at 15 Marina Boulevard on November 6, opening the path to demolition permits on one of the most contested development proposals in the neighborhood's recent history. The approved project calls for two mixed-use towers of 22 and 18 stories holding 848 apartments above a new, larger Safeway grocery store. Of those apartments, 86 would be reserved for low-income households.

Opponents wasted little time responding. On November 12, the YesAnd Foundation, Neighborhoods United SF, and four Marina residents filed an amended complaint in federal court asking a judge to set aside the approval entirely. The amended filing alleges that San Francisco Planning quietly dropped a hazardous-materials safeguard from its own review guidelines on the very day the project advanced to fast-track review — then granted final approval without those protections ever being restored. Plaintiffs also note that the city's own Property Information Map still listed the project as under review on November 10, four days after the official approval date. The lawsuit names Align Real Estate, the city's Planning and Public Health departments, PG&E, and Safeway parent company Albertsons as defendants.

Align has stated it will meet all environmental testing requirements, and city planners argue that additional soil assessments and any necessary remediation can be handled during the permitting phase. State regulators have concluded that known contamination on the site poses no current public-exposure risk.

The project has also drawn opposition from Mayor Daniel Lurie and District 2 Supervisor Stephen Sherrill, both of whom have questioned whether towers of this height belong in a neighborhood zoned for 40-foot buildings. Final planning approval does not mean construction is imminent: demolition and building permits are still required, and the pending federal litigation could delay or block the project before a shovel breaks ground.

topStories.headline: Magic Theatre Opens World Premiere of 'a Rashomon' at Fort Mason on November 18
topStories.dek: The Fort Mason new-works company brings a Kurosawa-inspired play set on San Francisco's own Market Street to the stage for a three-week run beginning Wednesday.
topStories.body:
Magic Theatre, the Fort Mason Center company that has been producing world premieres of new plays since its founding in 1967, opens 'a Rashomon' on Wednesday, November 18, with performances running through December 6. The play was conceived by Joan Osato and written by Ashley Smiley, and is directed by Edris Cooper-Anifowoshe. The cast includes Juan Amador, Nora el Samahy, Britney Frazier, and Jeuneé Simon.

The production borrows its narrative structure from Akira Kurosawa's 1950 film — multiple, contradictory accounts of a single violent event — and relocates the story to Market Street at the foot of San Francisco's cable-car turnaround. At the center of the narrative is the death of a Black dancer, a native son of the city who dies anonymously in his own streets. The production layers in puppets, a diorama of San Francisco, and original videography.

Magic Theatre is a designated San Francisco Legacy Business and one of the country's last theater companies dedicated exclusively to world-premiere new work. It has operated out of Landmark Building D at Fort Mason Center for Arts and Culture since 1977. Opening night is Wednesday, November 18, at 8:00 PM. The full schedule and tickets are available at magictheatre.org.

topStories.headline: Sherrill Begins Full Four-Year Term as District 2 Supervisor After November 3 Win
topStories.dek: Stephen Sherrill secured a full term representing Marina, Pacific Heights, Cow Hollow, and Presidio Heights, capping a year that began with a mayoral appointment and ended with a second decisive election victory.
topStories.body:
Stephen Sherrill was re-elected to a full four-year term as San Francisco's District 2 Supervisor on November 3, closing out a cycle that began with his appointment by Mayor London Breed in December 2024, continued with a June 2026 special-election win at 69 percent of the vote, and ended with another strong showing at the general election. District 2 covers the Marina District, Pacific Heights, Cow Hollow, and Presidio Heights.

Sherrill enters his new term with several housing and infrastructure priorities already in motion. He co-sponsored an Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District designed to unlock roughly 1,200 new housing units at 3333 and 3700 California Street in Presidio Heights. He also backed the November transit-funding measures — the local Stronger Muni for All parcel tax and the regional Connect Bay Area sales tax — and authored small-business legislation, passed unanimously by the Board, to allow retail stores into long-vacant commercial spaces across the district.

On the Safeway towers controversy — the defining land-use dispute of his first term — Sherrill has sided with neighbors who say the proposed 22- and 18-story buildings are out of scale with the surrounding waterfront neighborhood, though state housing law has sharply limited the city's legal ability to block the project outright.

moreNews.headline: Pod Gym The Yard Strength Training Coming to Union Street in Cow Hollow
moreNews.body: The Yard Strength Training, a Bay Area fitness company built around reservation-based private training pods, signed a lease for 4,300 square feet at 1906 Union Street in Cow Hollow earlier this year, with an opening planned for fall 2026. The location will include nine private squat-rack pods, four reservable pilates reformers, small-group classes, a coworking lounge, and discounted parking — the company's third Bay Area location overall. As of this week, The Yard's website lists the opening as forthcoming and says a confirmed date will be announced shortly.
